lines.text: Cosmo! Cosmo, wake up!
Your best friend Sprockle is shaking you awake, his antennae twitching like crazy.
I've been watching the galaxy all night, and something big is happening! Want me to tell you about it?
Oh! Okay, no rush.
Sprockle fiddles with his gadgets, bouncing on his toes.
But it's really, really important, Cosmo. The whole galaxy might depend on it! Ready to hear what I found?
That's okay, Cosmo. We'll save the galaxy another day. Get some rest, buddy.
Sprockle pulls out a glowing hologram map.

Okay, so here's the thing. Our galaxy, Nutria, used to have three planets. Frootopia, Vegonnia, and Zoomara. But then the Mucklars came. Dark, gloopy creatures. And they wiped out Vegonnia completely!
Should I tell you about the Mucklars?
Fair enough. The history stuff is scary anyway! Long story short: gloopy creatures, bad. Frootopia, good. And we've got the Great Froot Tree protecting us. You know, the tree you clean the pipes for!
Ooh, look, Gribbo just walked into the café. Want to go say hi?
Sprockle leans in close and lowers his voice.
A scientist called Gloomp found something called the Sludge Core on a dead planet. It changed him, Cosmo! It turned him and his followers into Mucklars, made of pure gloom.
Now only Frootopia is left, protected by the Great Froot Tree. And that's where you come in, pipe-cleaner extraordinaire!
Hey, Gribbo just walked into the café. Want to go say hi?
No worries, Gribbo's always around anyway.
Sprockle turns back to his gadgets. Suddenly, his Pingotron three thousand starts beeping like crazy!
Whoa, whoa, whoa! Cosmo, this is a signal from where Vegonnia used to be! Should we check it out?
Heyyy, Cosmo! Sprockle!
Gribbo waves a half-eaten space-mango. He's a goofy delivery driver who knows everyone in the galaxy. Next to him sits Tula, a fierce warrior from Vegonnia. She nods, but says nothing.
Suddenly, Sprockle's Pingotron starts beeping like crazy!
Guys! I'm picking up a signal from where Vegonnia used to be! Should we check it out?
The signal is definitely real! But nobody ever believes my readings.
Probably just space static, buddy.
That's your boss calling! Are you going to answer?
Yeah. Probably just another glitch.
Told ya!
But before anyone can relax, your communicator buzzes. Loudly.
That's your boss! Something's wrong, Cosmo. Are you going to answer?
You let it ring. It stops. Then it buzzes again, with a voicemail alert.
Cosmo, that's your boss! If it's an emergency, we can't ignore it! Will you call back?
Okay, okay, then I will!
Before you can stop him, Sprockle taps your communicator and calls your boss back. The line connects, and he pushes the device into your hands.
Cosmo, talk! Will you take the call?
You try to push the communicator away, but your boss's voice booms through anyway, on the emergency channel.
Cosmo! This isn't optional! The Great Froot Tree is in trouble!
We have to listen.
Emergency! A big pipe on the Great Froot Tree has been damaged in an attack! If the water stops flowing, the tree could fail, and maybe all of Frootopia with it!
Cosmo! This is what you do! You fix pipes! We have to help!
My ship's right outside. Should we go?
You hesitate. This is big. Sprockle squeezes your arm.
Cosmo, if the Great Froot Tree fails, everything fails.
Ship door's open, buddy. You in? Do we head out right now?
You freeze with one foot on the ramp, like you're posing for a heroic poster. The universe is not impressed.
If the Great Froot Tree stops flowing, everyone feels it, Cosmo. Can we please head out now?
Everyone piles into Gribbo's clunky, fruit-filled spaceship. Tula takes a seat without a word. Sprockle starts scanning for danger.
She's not pretty, but she flies! Mostly.
Here we go, Cosmo! Ready for takeoff?
Wait, you say. You check your pipe kit. The seals. The wrenches. The extra-bendy pipe-cleaner.
Good call! Better prepared than panicked.
Okay, okay! Are we launching now?
You check the seals on your pipe kit one more time. And then one more time, just to be sure. The engines rumble impatiently.
Every minute we sit here, we burn fuel, Cosmo. Shall we launch?
You're flying through space when suddenly, Gribbo drops a peach. It rolls across the floor, bonks a big red button, and switches off the stealth mode!
Gribbo! They can see us now!
A patrol of Mucklar ships spots you! Tula cracks her knuckles.
We fight, or we run. Your call, Cosmo. Do we fight them?
I've fought these creatures before. Hold on!
Tula grabs the controls and the ship zig-zags through the laser fire.
This is terrifying, but also awesome!
One Mucklar ship spins away in a puff of smoke! But more are coming.
There's an asteroid field ahead! We could lose them in there! Should we try it?
Not yet, you shout! Tula keeps fighting, longer than she should.
Cosmo! We can't do this forever! Dive into the asteroid field?
Warning lights flash across the cockpit, like the ship is having a disco at the worst possible time. The Mucklar shots are getting closer.
Asteroids. Now. Do we dive in?
Punch it, Gribbo, you yell!
The fruit ship's engines scream as you zoom toward an asteroid field. Mucklar shots whizz past the windows!
I'm gonna be sick!
Almost there! Keep going into the asteroids?
Pull up, you shout! Gribbo yanks the controls and the ship skims the edge of the asteroids instead.
A laser blast scorches the side of the ship!
Cosmo, we have to lose them! Go into the asteroids now?
The ship lurches as another blast scrapes the hull. Gribbo's snack tray floats off into the air.
Cosmo, those rocks are our only cover! Into the asteroids?
You wait too long. A Mucklar blast fizzles the engines, and your little fruit ship drifts to a stop. The Mucklars tow you away with a big sticky tractor beam.
Game over! Want to start the adventure again and try a different choice?
After a wild chase through the spinning rocks, you finally lose the Mucklars! The ship limps on, trailing smoke.
We made it! Barely!
Up ahead, you can see the damaged pipe, spraying water into space.
There it is. Ready to see the damage, Cosmo?
You take a second to breathe. Sprockle's antennae are still wobbling.
That was the scariest thing I've ever done.
Talking time is over. Pipe time. Ready to check the damage?
You stare at the broken pipe, misting water into space like the galaxy's saddest garden sprinkler.
Every second counts. Ready to check the damage?
Water from the Great Froot Tree is spraying everywhere! You look at the crack carefully. You can fix this. But you're missing a part.
This is your specialty, Cosmo! What do we need? Will you tell us?
You hesitate. Saying how bad it is out loud makes it feel real.
Cosmo. Tell us what you need, and we'll find it. Will you tell us?
Saying nothing is a great plan for fixing absolutely nothing. Sprockle steadies your elbow.
Just tell us the part, and we'll get it. Will you tell us?
We need a hydro-valve coupler, you explain.
Those are super rare!
I know a place. The underground market. Bit shady, but they have everything.
I don't like it. But we don't have a choice.
What do you think, Cosmo? Should we go to the underground market?
You search the floating junk nearby, but hydro-valve couplers are really rare. Precious time ticks away.
Cosmo, the tree's getting weaker! We need Gribbo's market!
The underground market it is. Ready to go?
You wait another moment, and the hissing from the pipe gets louder.
Cosmo, please. Can we go to the market now?
The pipe keeps hissing like a countdown with no off switch.
The underground market's gross, but it has parts. Also, at least three kinds of mystery smells. Shall we go?
The underground market is a maze of flickering lights and very suspicious characters. Sprockle sticks close to you.
I don't like this place.
This guy's got everything!
Gribbo leads you to a junk dealer's stall.
A hydro-valve coupler? Oh, I've got one. But it's not for sale. Not for money, anyway.
Not for money? Maybe we should hear what he wants. Should we listen to his offer, Cosmo?
No deals, you start to say. But Sprockle tugs your sleeve.
Cosmo, we need that part.
Listen to your friend. I don't want your money. I want a little wager.
Do you want to hear his offer?
You start to back away from the stall. The dealer's grin gets wider.
Leaving so soon? You haven't even heard my offer.
We can say no after we know what we're saying no to. Like reading the menu first! Hear his offer?
That coupler is my prized possession! But I'll bet it on a race. Beat my janitor robot through the sewer tunnels, and it's yours.
Sewer tunnels? Ewww!
I was born for this. Should I race, Cosmo?
Tula tries to haggle, but the dealer folds his arms.
No race, no part!
There's no other way, Cosmo. And Gribbo's actually really good at racing!
Come on, let me race! Can I?
You try to refuse again, but the dealer just shrugs.
Then good luck with your leaky tree.
Cosmo. Let me do this. Will you let me race?
Gribbo wipes his hands on his jacket and actually looks focused, which is honestly a bit alarming.
I'm fast. I'm lucky. And I want to help. Also, I did one warm-up stretch. Let me race?
Gribbo hops onto a rusty hover-scooter. The janitor robot revs its engine.
Ready? Go!
Sewer water sprays everywhere as Gribbo zooms through the pipes! He's neck and neck with the robot!
I can't watch! Cosmo, do you cheer for Gribbo?
You can't look. It's too gross, and too close. Sprockle peeks through his fingers.
Cosmo, look! He's still racing! Keep watching?
Congratulations, this is the grossest race in the history of the galaxy. The janitor robot pulls a little ahead.
Just tell me if he's winning! Keep watching?
In a photo finish, Gribbo wins by a nose!
Yee-haw!
He's covered in muck, but he's holding the hydro-valve coupler high!
He did it! Now you can fix the pipe, Cosmo! Ready to get to work?
You don't celebrate yet. The Great Froot Tree is still losing water.
Right. Fix first, party later. Ready to work?
Gribbo is still holding the coupler like a trophy. Then he remembers it's also the thing that saves everyone.
Cosmo. Ready to fix it?
You work fast. Sprockle passes you the tools, one by one.
The spray stops. The pipe is fixed, and the Great Froot Tree's water flows again! Everyone cheers!
Uh, Cosmo? There's an urgent message. Should we listen?
Not yet, you say. You just want one quiet second.
But the communicator buzzes again, even louder.
Cosmo, we have to hear it. Will you listen?
Your communicator is doing a tiny panic-dance in your pocket. One word flashes on the screen: Defense.
We really have to hear this. Listen?
All workers, report to the Great Froot Tree at once! Prepare to defend it from a Mucklar invasion!
But our ship got wrecked in that chase. We're not flying anywhere.
He kicks the smoking engine.
Should we figure out what to do next?
You stare at the smoking engine. For a moment, it feels hopeless. Sprockle nudges you.
Cosmo, you're the one who fixes things. Even impossible things. Will you try?
The engine coughs and spits smoke, like it just swallowed a hairball.
Start with what you know, Cosmo. Will you try?
Another signal! And this one's close!
A battered ship lands nearby. The markings are unmistakable. Veggonauts! Survivors from Vegonnia!
I thought they were all gone! Should we talk to them?
You hold back. What if it's a trap, you whisper?
Maybe. But they're Veggonauts. If they're alive, they have answers. Do we go and talk to them?
The ship's markings are definitely Veggonaut. Either they're friends, or someone made a really good trap costume.
We listen first. Then we decide. Shall we go over?
Listen to me, all of you. King Citrinus of Frootopia is secretly working with the Mucklars! He's calling every defender to the Great Froot Tree, to lead them into a trap!
The king? Cosmo, do you believe them?
How do we know this isn't a Mucklar trick?
The Veggonaut commander shows you recordings of their ruined home world.
We have nothing left to gain from lies.
That's pretty convincing, Cosmo. Do you believe them now?
You still don't want to believe it. The commander looks you right in the eye.
If you walk into that trap, you won't walk back out. Stay with us, and we can fight together.
Do you believe them?
You want it to be a trick. You really, really do. But the recordings are real, and the commander looks tired, not sneaky.
I trust them, Cosmo. Will you?
Thank you, Cosmo. We won't forget this.
The team decides not to walk into the king's trap.
But what do we do? We need help!
Then you have an idea. What about the Beastroos, on the planet Zoomara?
The Beastroos? They've never taken sides! Should we try?
You hate the idea of asking strangers for help.
Cosmo, if we don't find friends, we can't win. Head for Zoomara?
Asking the Beastroos for help makes your tummy twist like a pretzel. Sprockle points to the empty sky where Vegonnia used to be.
We can't do this alone. Should we fly to Zoomara?
The Veggonauts help repair the ship. But there's a problem.
We don't have enough fuel to reach Zoomara!
I saw an abandoned fuel capsule in the Dead Zone. But it's guarded by an ancient robot.
Sounds dangerous. But we have no choice. Should we go and find it?
An ancient robot, you repeat. That sounds like a bad day.
A bad day, but a necessary day. Shall we go and find the fuel?
We can't, you say. But then you hear it. Over the radio, a long, tired groan from the Great Froot Tree.
We don't get to stop, Cosmo. Go after the fuel?
You try to say no, but your feet start walking anyway. Tula doesn't argue. Gribbo follows. And Sprockle stays right by your side.
Come on, Cosmo.
In the Dead Zone, you find the ancient fuel capsule. A huge robot stands in front of it, eyes glowing.
Solve the riddle, or leave.
Sprockle hides behind you.
Riddles? I'm good at riddles! Want me to try?
No, you whisper. Let me think.
Okay! Okay! You are smart, Cosmo!
I have cities, but no houses. I have mountains, but no trees. I have water, but no fish. What am I?
Do you want me to answer after all?
You close your eyes and picture Sprockle's hologram map. Cities. Mountains. Water. But no houses, no trees, no fish. You open your eyes. A map, you say.
Correct.
Cosmo! You did it! Shall we grab the fuel?
I have cities, but no houses. I have mountains, but no trees. I have water, but no fish. What am I?
Sprockle's eyes light up. He tugs your sleeve.
Cosmo! I know this one! It's a map! Should I say it?
Hmm, maybe it's not a map. Is it a pizza?
Incorrect.
Wait! Wait! It is a map! A map!
The robot's eyes flicker, then glow green, and the capsule starts to open.
I should have trusted myself! Do you grab the fuel?
For a long second, the robot doesn't move. Its eyes flicker red, then green, then red again.
Did I mess up? Cosmo, do we grab the fuel and run?
Don't move.
Correctness verified.
Okay. Okay. We're fine.
With a hiss, the capsule opens. Inside is enough fuel to reach Zoomara and back!
Yes! We did it! High five!
Next stop, Zoomara! Ready to blast off, Cosmo?
You look at the fuel. This is really happening.
Zoomara could save us, Cosmo. Ready to fly there?
The fuel gauge is finally full. The ship goes quiet for a second, like the universe is holding its breath.
This next stop decides everything. Shall we go?
Zoomara is breathtaking. Ancient forests stretch on forever, glowing with magic.
Wow! It's beautiful! The Beastroos live down there. They're wild and wise, and they've never taken sides in any war.
Let's hope they listen. Ready to land?
Not yet, you say. Gribbo circles over the forest while Sprockle scans the trees.
Lots of movement down there. But we can't hover forever. Land now?
You circle again. Big shapes move under the trees. The landing gear clunks halfway down, then stops, like it's having second thoughts.
They're already watching us. Land now?
You creep through the forest as quietly as you can. But within minutes, you're surrounded! Huge Beastroo warriors step out of the trees, holding tall wooden staffs.
Cosmo! What do we do?
Tula reaches for her weapon, but you stop her. Should you try talking to them first?
Tula reaches for her weapon, but the Beastroos are impossibly fast. In seconds, the whole team is surrounded, with nowhere to go.
Bad idea! Bad idea!
Their leader, Shaman Pawra, steps forward.
Speak, and we may let you stay.
Cosmo, say something! Will you speak to her?
You stay silent. Shaman Pawra tilts her head, studying you like a puzzle.
Silence is also a choice.
Cosmo, maybe we should talk.
Last chance, small one. Will you speak from your heart?
Shaman Pawra is ancient and powerful, with eyes that seem to see right through you.
Speak, small one. But choose your words carefully.
You can do this, Cosmo. Just speak from your heart!
Will you take Sprockle's advice?

You take a deep breath. I'm just a pipe-cleaner, you say. I fix water pipes. I have a family waiting for me at home. But the darkness is coming for everyone. Vegonnia is gone. Frootopia is next. And then it will come here. We can't win alone. But together, we might have a chance.
That was beautiful, Cosmo.
Do you think your words reached them?

You keep it practical. I look after the Great Froot Tree's pipes, you say. I know how fragile life is when the water stops. If the Mucklars win, they won't stop at Frootopia. They'll drain every world. Help us, and I promise to protect your forest like it's my own.
He means it.
Shaman Pawra watches you carefully. Do you think it convinced her?
The forest stays quiet. Shaman Pawra raises a clawed hand.
Words are easy. Deeds are rare. A life-pipe from your Great Froot Tree runs under these woods. It is cracked, and leaking. Fix it, and we will believe you.
Cosmo, that's literally your job!
Will you accept the challenge?
You kneel by the cracked pipe. With steady hands, you seal it with tree resin, wire, and your trusty pipe-cleaning kit. The glow grows stronger. The whole forest seems to sigh with relief.
You mend what others break. We will send our swiftest hunters with you.
Yes! Ready to go back to Frootopia, Cosmo?
You lean back, tired. Your hands are still shaking from the repair.
Cosmo, let's go while Pawra's on our side. Back to Frootopia?
The forest is so calm, it feels like it's trying to sell you a nap. But Pawra's hunters are already gathering.
They won't wait forever. Back to Frootopia?
You hesitate. Tula steps forward, kneels, and lays her weapon on the ground.
I lost my world because nobody stood together. I won't let it happen again.
A warrior who bows is either wise, or desperate. We will send a small group of scouts. Earn the rest.
Better than nothing! Ready to go back to Frootopia?
You look back at the Beastroo scouts gathering in the trees.
We got something. It's enough.
Cosmo, we should move. Back to Frootopia?
The Beastroo scouts blend into the trees like salad ninjas.
We have to move before the trail goes cold. Back to Frootopia?
The forest goes silent. Shaman Pawra studies you for a long, long moment. Then she nods.
For the first time in a thousand years, the Beastroos will fight.
Yes! Cosmo, you did it! The Beastroos are with us! Ready to go back to Frootopia?
For a second, you don't move. The forest feels much safer than what comes next.
Frootopia needs you, Cosmo. Go back now?
The forest air smells fresh. Suspiciously fresh. But you can't stop thinking about the Great Froot Tree.
Home needs you. Go back now?
With the Beastroos on your side, you sneak back into Frootopia. King Citrinus is still sending out fake calls for help, telling everyone to gather at the Great Froot Tree.
It's definitely a trap. Tula knows the Captain of the Royal Guard. Should we contact him?
Not yet, you whisper.
Okay. Then what?
Every second we wait, the trap gets tighter. Do we contact the Captain now?
The king's broadcast echoes across the city. It's like a villain's TV advert. But wait, there's more!
We need the Captain before the trap closes. Contact him now?
Tula's old friend, the Captain of the Royal Guard, confirms everything. The king is trying to open an ancient, forbidden portal to the Mucklars' world!
Cosmo! I could hack into the city's speakers and warn everyone! Should I try?
I'm in!
Sprockle's message flashes on every communicator in the city, telling everyone about the king's betrayal! The people of Frootopia start to stand up against him.
Now let's stop that portal! Should we head to the Great Froot Tree?
Wait, you say. We need a plan.
But the portal's already opening! If we wait too long, we lose. Go to the tree now?
The Pingotron is beeping like a stressed-out hamster. The portal energy keeps climbing.
That number only goes one way, Cosmo. To the tree?
The team spreads out, warning people face to face. It's slow, but the news spreads.
I'm hacking in anyway, to make it louder! There! Now, to the Great Froot Tree! Ready?
You take one more minute to make sure everyone has heard the warning.
Cosmo, we have to move! To the tree?
The city is buzzing. Everyone's shouting, nobody's in charge, and somehow, everyone's looking at you.
If we don't stop that portal, none of this matters. To the tree?
A little robot lemonade seller called Robolade rolls up to you.
Lemonade? Fresh lemonade? No? Then how about a secret tunnel through the ancient pipes?
Those are the same pipes you look after, Cosmo! Just deeper, and older! Should we take the tunnel?
There's no other way. The king's guards are watching every street.
She's right. And you know pipes better than anyone! Will you lead us through the tunnel?
I don't know those tunnels, you admit.
But you know pipes better than anyone in the galaxy!
Lead us, Cosmo.
Will you lead the way?
The tunnel smells ancient and metallic, with just a hint of bad idea.
You're the pipe expert.
We'll follow you. Lead the way?
You lead the way through the twisting tunnels. Ancient carvings cover the walls.
These are from Frootopia's forgotten past!
At last, you climb out near the roots of the Great Froot Tree. And what you see is terrifying.
Cosmo, look! Should we look at what's happening?
You don't want to look. Not yet.
Cosmo, it's really bad. Will you look?
You can hear chanting up ahead. The air is humming.
Whatever's happening, it's happening right now. Look?
King Citrinus stands in front of the Great Froot Tree, arms raised. Dark energy crackles around an ancient portal, and it's already opening!
The portal! It's happening! Do we stop him now?
You wait, looking for the right moment. But the portal keeps growing!
It's now or never!
Tula charges forward, and the team follows.
Come on, Cosmo! Will you join the fight?
You try to hold back, but there's no time. Tula grabs your arm and pulls you along.
Stay close, Cosmo! Keep going?
A wave of gloomy darkness rolls out of the portal, and everybody gasps. Tula blocks a guard's staff, inches from your nose.
Don't stop now! Keep going?
You wait too long. The portal opens wide, the darkness pours out, and one by one, the lights of Frootopia go out.
Game over! Want to start the adventure again and try a different choice?
Stop, you shout! The king turns around, sneering.
Only through darkness can balance be restored! Guards, stop those pipe-cleaners!
Tula takes on the guards.
Cosmo! I have an idea! My experimental anti-gravity gun! Should I use it?
No, you shout, it's experimental!
Cosmo, we're running out of options! Can I use it?
Sprockle fumbles the anti-gravity gun as a guard closes in.
If this works, it changes everything. If it doesn't, we invent a brand new kind of panic. Can I use it?
Sprockle aims the anti-gravity gun at the king.
Come on, come on!
King Citrinus and his guards float up into the sky like balloons, spinning and shouting!
It worked! My invention actually worked!
Do you turn to look at the portal?
You watch the king spin away into the clouds. Okay, you think, that did work.
Cosmo! The portal! Will you look?
Behind you, the portal's hum turns into a roar, like an angry blender. The ground trembles.
Cosmo! Should we look at the portal?
But it's too late. The portal is wide open, and Mucklars pour out into Frootopia! Thousands of them! Shadowy, gloopy creatures, hungry for light.
No! What do we do? Cosmo, do we keep fighting?
The Beastroos have arrived! And behind them, the Veggonauts, and the loyal Frugglies of Frootopia!
They came! They really came!
But even with everyone, there are just too many Mucklars.
Cosmo, we need a plan! Do you have one?
Your mind goes blank. Too much noise. Too much darkness. Sprockle grabs your shoulders.
Cosmo! You're the reason we got this far. Think! Do you have an idea?
Mucklars surge forward like a tide of gloop. It's chaos, like a buffet where every dish is danger.
Cosmo, give us anything! Do you have any idea at all?
Yes! You keep fighting!
The Beastroos arrive, with the Veggonauts and the loyal Frugglies right behind them!
The allies! But there are still too many Mucklars. You're the smartest person I know, Cosmo! Do you have an idea?
I don't know, you shout over the noise!
Then make a decision!
Sprockle looks at you like you're the last light in the galaxy. Do you come up with an idea?
Cosmo! Now!
The Beastroos roar in the distance. Sprockle looks terrified. Do you have an idea?
You have an idea! You're a pipe-cleaner. You know every pipe that connects to the Great Froot Tree!
Cosmo! What is it?
I can reroute one of the ancient light pipes, you explain, and send the tree's pure life energy across the battlefield!
That's brilliant! Will you try it?
What if I break it, you shout?
Cosmo, pipes are your life! If anyone can do it, it's you! Will you try?
The ancient pipe junction is right in front of you, warm with the tree's energy, like a hot water bottle with cosmic powers. Your hands hover over the valves.
If anyone can do it, it's you. Try it?
You work the pipes like only you can. Pure light surges through the ancient system and bursts across the battlefield!
The Mucklars fizzle into harmless puffs of smoke! Wave after wave, gone! Even Lord Gloomp shrinks into a tiny, squeaking puddle of goo!
You did it, Cosmo!
But the portal is still open. Do you check what's on the other side?
You don't celebrate. Not while the portal is still breathing dark air.
What's next, Cosmo? Should we check the portal?
The battlefield is bright with victory. But the portal is still open, still humming, like it missed the we-won announcement.
Check the portal?
On the other side of the portal, the Sludge Core is still glowing. Someone has to carry a jar of Froot Tree essence through, and destroy it. But the portal is wobbly. It might be a one-way trip.
Cosmo, who would volunteer for that? Will anyone?
Nobody should have to, you whisper. The portal crackles, like it's listening.
But if nobody goes, the darkness comes back. Will anyone volunteer?
The portal spits black sparks. Sprockle looks at the glowing jar, then at you.
It's a one-way job. No refunds. No returns. Will anyone volunteer?
Then Gribbo steps forward.
I'll do it. Someone's gotta, right?
Gribbo, no!
But Gribbo has already picked up the glowing jar.
Cosmo, we can't let him go alone! Should we follow him through?
You hesitate at the edge of the portal. Then Sprockle takes your hand.
Together, Cosmo. Always together.
One by one, the team steps up behind Gribbo.
Here we go. Into Morbia. Ready?
At the edge of the portal, you stop. The air on the other side feels wrong. Sprockle squeezes your hand.
I'm scared too. Do we go in?
The air at the portal goes cold and oily. Morbia smells like rust and thunder.
We go together. Enter Morbia?
You turn away from the portal. Behind you, the Sludge Core keeps glowing, and the darkness keeps growing. This time, there's no second chance.
Game over! Want to try again?
Morbia is a nightmare. Bubbling sludge pools. Twisted grey rocks. And in the middle, pulsing like a dark heartbeat, the Sludge Core.
I don't like this place.
As you get closer, the Core fights back, filling everyone's heads with scary pictures.
Fight it, Cosmo! Can you push through?
For a second, you freeze. The air feels heavy.
Cosmo! Stay with me!
Move!
Gribbo takes a shaky step forward, holding the glowing jar. Will you push through the fear?
You can't move. Sprockle and Tula pull you forward anyway, one step at a time.
Cosmo, I need you back. Will you keep going?
The fear wins. Your knees wobble, and a big wave of sludge washes the whole team back through the portal. It slams shut behind you, with the Sludge Core still glowing on the other side.
Cosmo?
Game over! Want to jump back in and try again?
You see your family in danger. Tula sees Vegonnia falling again. Sprockle sees all of his inventions breaking. But he shakes his head.
It's not real! None of it is real!
And Gribbo, snack-loving Gribbo, keeps walking forward. Do you cheer him on?
Gribbo stumbles. His knees buckle, and the glowing jar wobbles in his hands.
Gribbo!
Cosmo, decide! Does Gribbo keep the jar?
You can show me anything you want! I'm still gonna throw this!
Do it, Gribbo!
With all his strength, Gribbo throws the jar of Froot Tree essence at the Sludge Core! Cosmo, do you shout for it to hit?
You grab the jar from Gribbo. I've got it, you shout, squinting through the scary haze.
Cosmo, be careful!
Your hands are shaking. Do you throw it now?
The jar whips past the Sludge Core and smashes on the rocks, splashing glowing essence everywhere! The Core shrieks, but it's still there!
There's one more jar! We only get one more chance! Cosmo, will you throw this one yourself?
Light meets dark in a huge flash! The Sludge Core collapses in on itself! And behind you, the portal starts to close!
Run! Come on, Cosmo! We have to get out! Do you run for the portal?
Now, you shout! You throw with everything you've got, and it hits!
The Sludge Core collapses with a horrible squelch! But the portal is closing even faster!
We have seconds! Do we sprint for it?
You hesitate for half a heartbeat, and the closing portal roars louder. The ground shakes under your feet.
Move!
Don't stop, Cosmo! Dive for the portal?
You dive just in time and tumble onto the ground on the other side, bumped and bruised.
The portal snaps shut with a thunderclap.
Cosmo! You're okay!
Then his smile disappears.
Wait. Where's Gribbo? Is he gone?
You, Sprockle and Tula dive through the shrinking portal, just in time!
It snaps shut behind you.
Gribbo? Gribbo! Cosmo, is he gone?
Wait! The rubble moves! A hand pops out, covered in glowing fruit goo. It's Gribbo! Dazed, but okay!
Did I miss anything?
Gribbo! You're okay! Cosmo, he's okay!
The crowd goes wild! Is this a happy ending?
For a moment, everyone is very, very quiet. Sprockle hides his face in your shoulder.
Then the rubble moves! Gribbo stumbles out, covered in glowing fruit goo!
Did I miss anything?
Gribbo! Cosmo, he made it!
Everyone cheers! Is this a happy ending?
You breathe out. But something feels different. Everyone is safe, but they're tired and bruised, and staring at the sky where the portal used to be.
We won, Cosmo. But it was hard.
Do you still want to celebrate a happy ending?
The cheering is real. But so is the quiet after it. Tula looks away, blinking hard. Gribbo laughs, then winces.
We got him back, Cosmo. And we did it.
Do you want to hear what happens next?
With the darkness gone and the portal sealed forever, the people of Nutria come together at last. Frugglies, Veggonauts and Beastroos join to form the Republic of Frootopia!
We did it, Cosmo. We really did it.
Want to hear what happens to our heroes?

You go home to your family, a hero. Sprockle's inventions finally get the attention they deserve, and he becomes Chief Scientist! Tula leads the new defense force of the united planets. And Gribbo gets all the snacks he can eat!
But best of all? You and Sprockle still meet at the café every morning. And the Great Froot Tree glows brighter than ever.
That was amazing, Cosmo!
The end!
The galaxy of Nutria is at peace. The Great Froot Tree glows brighter than ever. And somewhere, in a cozy little café, you and Sprockle are already planning your next adventure.
That was fun, Cosmo!
The end!
But that's not quite the end. That night, Gribbo hangs his jacket on a chair at the café, and heads home.
The café is dark, and quiet. And then, deep in the jacket pocket, something tiny and golden opens its eyes.
Pip?
To be continued...
Previously, in Frootopia: Cosmo and his friends smashed the Sludge Core, sent the Mucklars packing, and saved the Great Froot Tree.
Everyone went home happy. But that night, Gribbo's jacket pocket began to glow...
The Kingdom of Frootopia. Story two: The Stowaway.
It's the morning after the big battle. The café is full of yawning heroes, and Gribbo has just pulled on the jacket he left on his chair last night.
Morning, everybody! Who wants a celebration doughnut?
But then his jacket pocket starts to wriggle. And glow.
Uh, Gribbo? Your pocket is glowing. Should we look inside?
You don't need to. The pocket pops open all by itself!
Out tumbles a tiny golden fluffball, with enormous sparkly eyes and one little leaf on top of its head.
Pip!
It's adorable! Gribbo, where did you get it?
No idea! I just found it in my pocket! Hey, it's looking at you, Cosmo. Do you hold out your hand?
You keep your hands in your pockets. But the little critter doesn't mind. It hops onto your head, slides down your nose, and lands in your hand!
Pip!
The little critter snuggles into your hand. It's warm, like holding a tiny sun.
Pip! Pip! Pip!
It only says one word! Should we call it Pip?
Pip it is! Pip bounces so high it nearly hits the ceiling.
Pip!
Pip disagrees. Very loudly. So, Pip it is!
Then Pip's tummy rumbles.
It zooms across the café and gobbles up every single snack!
My emergency doughnuts!
Pip giggles, and flowers burst out of every cup in the café!
My Pingotron is going wild! This little thing is full of energy! Cosmo, can we keep Pip?
Pip curls up on the counter and purrs. It's not going anywhere!
Suddenly, the lights flicker, the café goes cold, and a huge hologram fizzes up in the middle of the room.
Good morning, Frootopia. I am Admiral Rot. You have something that belongs to me. That little creature. Hand it over.
Pip...
Cosmo, he wants Pip! Do we hand Pip over?
You hold Pip out toward the hologram. And Pip's little lip wobbles.
Pip?
You can't do it! You tuck Pip safely behind your back.
Not today, Admiral! Pip's our friend now.
Then I shall come and take it. Tonight! After my bath.
The hologram fizzles out. Everyone looks at Pip. Pip looks at everyone.
We need to hide it. Somewhere nobody would ever look.
Your house, Cosmo! Nobody ever suspects a pipe-cleaner! Should we hide Pip at your house?
You think of other places. The sewer? Too smelly. The market? Too shady. Your house it is!
At your house, you hide Pip in the fruit bowl, right between an apple and an orange. The perfect disguise!
But your little sibling spots Pip straight away, and dresses it up in a tiny bow and a party hat.
Pip! Pip!
Cosmo? Why is the fruit bowl glowing?
Uh... it's a very healthy fruit bowl!
Pip gives a tiny yawn. Do you make Pip a cosy little bed?
You make a bed out of a slipper and a sock. Pip snuggles right in.
Pip.
Pip makes its own bed. In Gribbo's hat.
Fair enough.
Later that night, the house is quiet. Pip is curled up like a tiny glowing nightlight.
Rot said tonight. I'll keep watch.
Outside, something goes squelch. Then squelch again.
What was that? Cosmo, do you keep watch with Tula?
You tiptoe over and peek out of the window with Tula. Nothing moves... until something does.
You pull a blanket over your head. But Tula taps you on the shoulder.
They're here.
Suddenly, the front door bursts open! In waddle the Mouldies: fuzzy grey-green blobs with runny noses.
And they're sneezing fuzzy spores everywhere! One of them politely wipes its feet.
Rot's minions! They're after Pip! Do we protect Pip?
You jump in front of Pip, brave as anything!
Gribbo grabs a frying pan. Sprockle grabs... a spoon.
You freeze. But Pip doesn't.
Pip starts to glow. Brighter... and brighter...
Piiiip!
Flash! A burst of golden light knocks every Mouldy flat on its back!
Whoa! The little guy packs a punch!
Pip flops down, worn out. And the Mouldies are already wobbling back up.
We have to go. Now. If Pip goes, they'll follow, and leave your house alone. Do we run for Gribbo's ship?
More squelching outside! There's no time to argue. Gribbo grabs Pip, and everyone runs!
You all pile into Gribbo's clunky little ship, and blast off into the night.
She's not pretty, but she flies! Mostly. Music, anyone?
Gribbo switches on the radio. A funky space tune starts playing, and Pip starts to dance on the dashboard!
Look at it go! Cosmo, do you dance too?
You dance like nobody's watching! Pip copies every single move.
You just tap your foot. So Sprockle dances instead. Badly. Very badly.
Then the music stops. The radar beeps. Mould ships! A whole fleet of them, right behind you!
Rot's face fizzes onto the screen.
You cannot outrun me, pipe-cleaner.
Oh, can't we? Hold on to your antennae! Should I do a loop-the-loop?
Gribbo pulls back on the stick. Round and round you go! And two Mould ships crash right into each other!
Gribbo does one anyway. Oops. Everyone ends up on the ceiling.
But more ships keep coming. Zap! A laser hits the back of the ship.
They're too fast. We can't lose them out here.
Pip hops down onto a crate of fruit and stares at it. Its leaf is twitching.
I think Pip has an idea! Should we let Pip try something?
But Pip is already trying something. Pip is very stubborn.
Pip closes its eyes and glows. A tiny green shoot pops out of the crate.
Then it grows. And grows! A giant vine bursts out of the hatch, and tangles up the Mould ships like spaghetti!
Yee-haw! Take that, fuzzballs!
Pip looks very proud of itself. Do you give Pip a high five?
You hold up your hand. Pip bounces up and high-fives it with its whole body!
Pip!
So Pip high-fives itself. With its leaf.
Everything goes quiet. You float through space under a million stars.
Pip giggles at something only Pip can see. And for a moment, every star in the sky twinkles a little brighter.
Did you see that? When Pip laughed, the stars shone brighter! That's impossible. Isn't it? Cosmo, do you think Pip made the stars shine?
You nod. Sprockle writes it down in his notebook. Very important science.
You shrug. Probably a coincidence. Sprockle writes it down too. Just in case.
Then, thump! Something lands on the roof.
The hatch creaks open, and down drops a stranger in shiny gold armour, with a dark helmet hiding its face.
The creature. Hand it over.
Not a chance.
Cosmo! Do we stand up to the stranger?
Tula leaps forward with her staff! But the stranger is far too fast.
You try to hide Pip behind your back. But the stranger is far too fast.
Whoosh! The stranger scoops Pip into a glass jar, fires up a jetpack, and zooms out through the hatch!
Pip! Pip!
Through the window, you watch the jetpack streak away toward a gigantic grey-green moon. A moon covered in fuzz.
Moons don't have engines! It's a battle station! The Mould Moon!
Hang on, little buddy. We're coming.
To be continued...
Previously, in Frootopia: a tiny golden critter called Pip tumbled out of Gribbo's pocket. Admiral Rot wanted Pip for himself.
And a masked stranger snatched Pip away, to Rot's giant battle station: the Mould Moon.
The Kingdom of Frootopia. Story three: The Mould Moon.
Gribbo's ship creeps closer to the Mould Moon. It's enormous, and fuzzy, and it smells like old socks, even from out here.
I've scanned it. Every door is guarded. But there's one way in that isn't. The waste pipes.
Of course it's the waste pipes.
Cosmo knows pipes better than anyone. Cosmo, will you lead the way in?
Sprockle tries to lead instead. He gets lost three times before he even leaves the ship. You'd better lead.
You squeeze in through a rusty hatch, and drop into a giant pipe. Squelch. Everything is grey, and green, and very, very fuzzy.
Ugh! It smells like a giant's armpit in here!
Then you hear a tiny sniffling sound. Behind a pipe sits a baby Mouldy, all alone. It's lost.
Aww. It's one of Rot's, though. Cosmo, do you help the baby Mouldy?
You kneel down beside it. Gribbo gives it a crumb of his snack. The baby Mouldy gobbles it up.
It sneezes a happy little sneeze, and points down the pipe. That way!
You walk on. But it follows you, sniffling.
So Gribbo gives it a snack. It sneezes a happy little sneeze, and points down the pipe. That way!
Suddenly, clang! The hatch behind you slams shut. And the walls start to move.
The walls are closing in! I'm too young to be a sandwich!
Cosmo! There's a valve on the wall! Do you turn it?
You hesitate. The walls creak closer. Gribbo squeaks. Okay, okay! You grab the valve!
You heave on the valve. It squeals, and spins, and the walls grind to a stop. Then slowly, they slide back.
Phew. Still not a sandwich.
The pipe leads into a long corridor. And at the end of it stand two Mouldy guards.
Leave this to me. I came prepared. Cosmo, should I wear my disguise?
Gribbo is already wearing it. He's very proud of it.
Gribbo, now in a fuzzy Mouldy costume, waddles right up to the guards.
Evening, fellow Mouldies. Just three more Mouldies here. Totally normal Mouldies.
The guards nod. It's working! And then, Gribbo's nose begins to twitch.
Ah... ah... ACHOO!
That's not a Mouldy sneeze. Mouldies go pffft.
They know! Cosmo, do we run?
Gribbo tries a Mouldy sneeze. Pffft. It's terrible. Okay, now you run!
You run! Round corners, down ladders, and through a door marked: Absolutely No Entry.
My Pingotron's picking up Pip's glow! In here!
In the middle of the room is a huge, clunky machine. And in a glass jar on top is Pip! The machine is sucking out Pip's glow.
And through the window, one by one, the stars begin to flicker out.
Pip...
We have to stop that machine. Cosmo, do you smash it?
You look for an off switch. There isn't one. Not even a tiny one. Smashing it is!
You grab your biggest wrench, and give the machine a mighty whack! Bolts pop. Dials spin. The machine coughs, and sparks, and breaks!
But before you can reach Pip's jar, there's a whoosh of a jetpack.
Step away from the jar.
You again. Cosmo, should I fight the stranger?
Tula doesn't wait for permission.
Clack! Tula's staff meets the stranger's glowing staff! Clack! Clack! Then, with one last spin, Tula knocks the helmet clean off!
And underneath is... King Citrinus!
Ah. Hello. Fancy seeing you here.
King Citrinus! We thought you floated away for good!
Citrinus slumps to the floor. He looks very small, and very tired. Do you give him a hand up?
You don't. But from inside the jar, Pip squeaks at you.
Pip!
You sigh. And you help him up.
Citrinus stares at your hand. Then he takes it.
Nobody's ever helped me up before.
Rot promised me a crown bigger than a planet, if I caught your little friend. I'm sorry.
He pulls out a little golden key, and opens Pip's jar. Pip flops out into your hands. Its glow is very, very dim.
Pip.
Rot will be here any second. Go!
Cosmo, can we trust him? Do you trust Citrinus?
You're not sure. But Pip glows a tiny bit brighter when it looks at him. Pip trusts him. That's good enough.
Intruders! Every Mouldy to the machine room! Bring me that creature!
I'll hold the door. Go back down the pipes. Quickly!
For the first time in his whole life, King Citrinus is being brave. Do you say thank you to Citrinus?
You say thank you. Citrinus blinks. Nobody's ever thanked him before, either.
You're welcome. Now go!
Pip pip.
Pip squeaks a tiny thank you instead. Citrinus smiles.
You race back down into the pipes. Behind you, a hundred Mouldies are coming, sneezing all the way.
Then you spot the biggest valve you've ever seen.
That's the master valve for every sludge tank on the Mould Moon! If it opens, nobody will be able to follow us! Cosmo, will you open it?
Gribbo trips over his costume and bumps right into the valve. It opens! Oops.
The great wheel spins, and spins. Deep inside the Mould Moon, something starts to gurgle. And bubble. And rumble.
Time to go! The ship's at the end of this pipe! Is everybody ready to fly?
Ready or not, a wave of sludge is coming. Hold on tight!
Gribbo's ship zooms down the biggest pipe on the Mould Moon, dodging bolts and fuzz and flying sludge.
You burst out into space just as... boom! Every sludge tank pops at once, and the Mould Moon spins away like a giant fuzzy top!
You fools! You don't even know what that creature is!
We did it! We got Pip back! Cosmo, do you cheer?
Everyone cheers! Gribbo honks the horn three times.
Pip gives a tiny cheer for you.
Pip!
Back home, you tuck Pip into its little bed. But Pip doesn't bounce. Pip doesn't giggle.
Pip's glow fades. Then it flickers. And through the window, a star flickers too.
Cosmo. My readings. Every time Pip flickers, a star goes out.
Then we find a way. Together.
To be continued...
Previously, in Frootopia: Cosmo and his friends rescued Pip from the Mould Moon, with a little help from King Citrinus.
But Pip is fading. And every time Pip flickers, a star goes out.
The Kingdom of Frootopia. Story four: The Edge of Everything.
The next morning, the sky over Frootopia is strangely grey. Pip hasn't moved from its little bed.
Then there's a knock at the door. It's Shaman Pawra, all the way from the forests of Zoomara!
The forest whispered to me, small one. The stars are going out. Have you seen something glowing?
Cosmo, do you show Pip to Pawra?
Pip peeks out of its little bed all by itself. Pawra gasps.
This is no ordinary creature. Come. The old tunnels under the Great Froot Tree. The carvings will know.
You hurry through the streets with Pip in your hands.
And who should roll up, but your old friend Robolade.
Lemonade? Fresh lemonade? No? Then how about a secret tunnel? Again?
Robolade knows a secret tunnel! Do we take it?
Robolade beeps sadly. Then it opens the secret tunnel for you, just in case.
You lead the way through the twisting tunnels, all the way down to the ancient carvings.
The carvings from Frootopia's forgotten past! We saw these on our very first adventure!
And as you carry Pip closer, the carvings start to glow.
Closer, small one. Will you hold Pip up to the carvings?
Pip leans toward them all by itself, as if they're calling to it.
The carvings light up into a map of the stars. In the middle is a tiny seed with a leaf on top, surrounded by friends.
Every thousand years, the ruler of the universe becomes small again, and grows up again, with friends. When the little one fades, carry it to the Edge of Everything, before the last star goes out.
A little seed, with a leaf on top? Wait a minute... No. That's silly.
Cosmo, should we go to the Edge of Everything?
Pip flickers. Somewhere far away, another star goes out. There's no time to lose.
Pawra goes home to gather the Beastroos, and the rest of you blast off, following the star map to the edge of space.
The map leads to a giant stone gate floating in space. And it's guarded by someone you've met before.
Solve the riddle, or leave. What gets bigger, the more you share it?
Ooh! Ooh! I know this one! Cosmo, should I answer?
A sandwich?
Wrong. Very wrong. Sprockle had better answer.
A smile! A smile gets bigger, the more you share it!
Correct.
The old runes blaze with light, and the gate swings open. Beyond it is the deepest, darkest part of space.
Go, small ones. Protect the little light.
The deepest, darkest part of space. Cosmo, do we fly through?
Pip flickers in your hands. That settles it. Let's go.
You fly through the gate. It's quiet. Too quiet.
Then, out of the dark, comes the whole Mould Fleet. They've been waiting for you.
Did you really think I'd let you go, pipe-cleaner? The creature is mine.
Not without a fight. Cosmo, do we fight back?
Tula fires the ship's fruit cannon. Splat! A watermelon knocks one Mould ship away. But there are just too many.
There are too many of them! We can't fight them all!
Then a battered carrot-shaped ship swoops in beside you. It's the Veggonaut Commander!
Need a lift, Cosmo?
Everyone, into the carrot ship. I'll set my old girl on autopilot. She'll lead them away, like a decoy.
She's not pretty. But she flies. Mostly.
Do you say goodbye to Gribbo's ship?
You pat the dashboard. Thank you, ship. And the ship gives one happy little beep.
Gribbo says goodbye for everyone. He's not crying. It's just space dust in his eye.
Gribbo's little ship zooms off on its own, and the whole Mould Fleet follows it, far away into the dark.
And then, it's gone.
Gribbo pulls a stripy towel out of his pocket, and dabs his eyes.
I always pack a towel. You never know.
Do you give Gribbo a hug?
You give Gribbo a big hug. Then Sprockle joins in. Then Tula. It's a group hug.
Thanks, buddy.
Pip wobbles over and gives Gribbo the tiniest cuddle. Gribbo smiles.
Suddenly, the carrot ship coughs. Then it splutters. Then something under the floor hisses.
A fuel pipe's cracked! If it breaks, we'll never reach the Edge. Can anybody here fix pipes?
Can anybody fix pipes? Cosmo, can you fix it?
Everyone looks at you. You are the only pipe-cleaner for a billion miles. So you fix it.
A twist of your wrench, a tap of your hammer, and the engine purrs again. Pipe-cleaning saves the day!
But on the dashboard, Pip curls up tight. A soft golden cocoon wraps all the way around it, with Pip's little leaf poking out of the top.
It's... changing!
Keep it safe, Cosmo. Do you hold the cocoon?
You lift the cocoon very gently. It's still a little bit warm.
The cocoon wobbles toward the edge of the dashboard. You catch it just in time!
At last, you reach it. The Edge of Everything. Behind you, only one star is still shining: the very last star.
And in front of you, the stars just stop. There's nothing. Just a soft, shimmering, pearly nothing.
Except for one thing. An ancient stone door, covered in glowing stars.
A door at the end of the universe. Cosmo, do you knock?
You walk up to the door, and raise your hand to knock.
You're a bit nervous. Who knocks on a door at the end of the universe?
But before anyone can knock, a tall figure steps out of the shadows.
A thousand years I have waited for this moment.
Admiral Rot snatches the cocoon right out of your hands. The door swings open, and he steps through.
Slam!
Nobody slams a door on our little buddy.
To be continued...
Previously, in Frootopia: a tiny golden critter called Pip tumbled out of Gribbo's pocket, and Admiral Rot wanted Pip for himself.
Now Pip is fading, the stars are going out, and Rot has carried Pip's cocoon through a door at the very edge of the universe.
The Kingdom of Frootopia. Story five: The Last Star.
You push the door. You pull the door. Gribbo even tries talking to the door.
Pretty please?
It won't budge. And behind you, the very last star begins to flicker.
We can't open it on our own.
Then we don't do it on our own! Cosmo, do you call every friend you've ever made?
Sprockle is already pressing the big red button on his Pingotron.
Calling everyone! Everyone everywhere!
And they come! The Beastroos, with Shaman Pawra! The Veggonauts! The Frugglies of Frootopia!
The junk dealer and his janitor robot. Robolade. The old riddle robot. Even the baby Mouldy from the pipes!
And last of all...
Wait for me! I brought Rot's spare key!
Cosmo, Citrinus wants to help. Do you let him?
You remember how Pip trusted him. So you do too.
Citrinus turns the key. Everyone pushes, all together. And slowly, the door at the end of the universe swings open.
Warm, golden light pours out.
Pip is in there. Cosmo, do we go in?
Shaman Pawra gently takes your hand.
Together, small one.
Inside is a hall made of starlight. At the far end stands a great glowing throne. The Throne of Everything. And it's empty.
Beside it stands Admiral Rot, holding the cocoon, with a gang of Mouldies.
Welcome to the end of everything, pipe-cleaner. Would you like to hear a secret?
Rot tells you anyway. Villains love telling secrets.
I was the ruler's own guard. When the ruler became a tiny seed, I locked it inside the Sludge Core, so it could never grow up, and I could rule instead! Only the throne won't let me sit on it.
The gloom that leaked out of it made your Mucklars. And your silly lemon king did everything I told him.
Hey!
The cocoon in Rot's arms glows, very faintly. Do you tell Rot to give it back?
Give it back, you shout! Your voice echoes all around the hall.
You don't need to. Everyone else shouts it for you!
Never! Mouldies! Attack!
The battle begins! Beastroos bounce! Veggonauts zap! Frugglies throw fruit!
And far behind you, the very last star flickers. It's almost out.
Cosmo! The cocoon! Do you go for it?
Gribbo gives you a friendly push.
Go on, buddy! We've got this!
You run! Gribbo throws his trusty towel. It tangles around Rot's feet, and he trips!
The cocoon flies up into the air, and you catch it!
But it's cold. And dim. Do you tell Pip it's not alone?
You hold the cocoon close, and whisper. You're not alone, Pip. We're all here.
You can't find the words. But your friends can.
We're here, Pip!
We're right here, little buddy!
We're with you.
Even the baby Mouldy squeaks. And the cocoon begins to glow. Then it begins to crack.
FLASH! Out of the cocoon blooms something enormous, and golden, and glowing. As big as a moon, crowned with stars.
Cosmo... is that... Pip?
It is! Those are Pip's sparkly eyes. And that's Pip's little leaf, right on top.
A little seed with a leaf... not silly at all!
It doesn't look like Pip. Until it winks at you, with Pip's sparkly eyes. And there, right on top, is Pip's little leaf.
A little seed with a leaf... not silly at all!
Hello, Cosmo. It's me.
The little seed. The ruler of the universe.
Remember the signal, on the very first morning? The one nobody believed? That was me, calling for help from the dark. Sprockle believed. And you came.
And when the Sludge Core broke, I woke up and hid in Gribbo's pocket. I kept him safe, all the way home.
So that's why I came out glowing!
I knew it! I knew my readings were right!
Do you say hello to Pip?
Hi, Pip! you say. And Pip laughs a laugh so big, it shakes the stars.
You're far too amazed to speak. So Pip just beams at you.
Pip glows, and sends out a wave of golden light. One by one, every star in the universe blazes back on. Even the very last one.
Admiral Rot is trembling.
Your Majesty...
Does Admiral Rot deserve a second chance?
Pip smiles.
Everyone does.
Everyone deserves a second chance, Cosmo. Even him.
You were lonely, Rot. For a thousand years, all alone, guarding an empty chair. You don't have to be lonely any more.
I'm sorry. I'm so very sorry.
And the Mouldies give a fuzzy little cheer. Do you shake hands with Admiral Rot?
You shake Rot's hand. It's a little bit fuzzy.
The baby Mouldy gives Rot a hug instead. And Rot hugs it back.
And now, some presents.
Far away, Tula's home planet, Vegonnia, grows back! Broccoli forests, carrot towers, every sprout.
And for the first time ever, Tula smiles.
And zooming through the door, with one happy little beep, comes Gribbo's old ship, good as new!
She's still not pretty. But she's home!
Pip has one last surprise. Do you want to see it?
Too late! Pip has never kept a surprise for more than one second.
Pip shrinks, smaller and smaller, until it's tiny little Pip again, right in your hand.
Looking after the universe means looking after everyone. I can do that from right here. With my friends.
Shaman Pawra lifts Pip up high, for everyone to see. And the whole hall cheers.
Shall we all go home now?
Gribbo's tummy rumbles. Loudly. Home it is. Breakfast time!
